prompt: Find the volume of a box with dimensions $1 \times 3 \times 5$.
hint: The volume of a box comes from multiplying its three dimensions. One of these dimensions makes the work very short.

hints.text: The volume of a box comes from multiplying its three dimensions. One of these dimensions makes the work very short.
Set up $1 \times 3 \times 5$. Multiplying by $1$ changes nothing, so you only need $3 \times 5$.
$1 \times 3 \times 5 = 15$, so the volume of the box is $15$ cubic units.

explanation: The volume of a box is length times width times height: $V = 1 \times 3 \times 5$.
Multiplying by $1$ leaves a number unchanged, so $1 \times 3 = 3$.
Then multiply by the last dimension: $3 \times 5 = 15$.
The volume of the box is $15$ cubic units.
